answer: The canyon report publishes the merge explicitly at each forge. Each collapsed cluster gets one copper weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 120 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 72 times the capital for one share. A farm of 1316 identities would post 978 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
